findings: BLOCKER: validate_recipe_data accepts recipes whose only write-capable node or sole final surface-binding node is inactive for the standard profile (for example minimum_profile=high-risk). A standard task can therefore bypass its write lane or terminal source binding and still derive succeeded. Require at least one standard-active writer and a standard-active final binder, and add negative recipe/profile regressions.

BLOCKER: live-claim staleness compares only the cooperative owner label. Releasing/reacquiring PROC-999 under the same label in a sibling worktree allowed show and begin to succeed without resume while state.branch/worktree remained bound to the old claim. Bind and compare the exact claim generation (for example claimed_at or a claim-record digest) plus owner/branch/worktree in show, transitions, and abort; add same-label same-worktree and sibling-worktree handoff regressions.

BLOCKER: the review surface is not frozen. Node surface_digest is populated only by finalize, so source edits after freeze_diff and after architecture/verification/docs review can be absorbed by finalize and the graph can report succeeded for an unreviewed final surface. Capture the post-write/freeze digest and reject downstream begin/finish/finalize when it changes until the write lane is reopened; add a source-change-after-review regression.

BLOCKER: show/list take no work-graph lock. A reader can observe the normal event-append to projection-replace window and fail with state/event projection mismatch; a deterministic delayed-write probe reproduced this while the writer completed normally. Serialize read snapshots under the graph lock or implement a bounded consistent-read retry, with a concurrency regression.

ROBUSTNESS: CLI task IDs are interpolated into Git-common-dir state/event paths without task_claim.TASK_ID_RE validation. Reject invalid IDs before resolving graph paths and add a traversal-shaped negative CLI test.
untested_surfaces: Automatic replay/repair after a real process crash between event append and projection replacement remains intentionally absent; schema v1 only detects the persistent mismatch.
No matched single-agent defect-recall, false-positive, human-time, latency, or model-cost baseline was run, so this review makes no efficiency claim.
